why: A (universes 0; IsGeodesicFrom/expDom/exp definitions: exp_q v = γ(1) for a chosen geodesic γ on an open (-δ,1+δ) with γ0=q, γ'0=v, junk q): exp_q v = γ(1) for every such γ, exp_q 0 = q (q ∈ N), exp_q(tv) = γ(t) on (-δ,1+δ), a geodesic on (0,1) that is a smooth curve in N is the ray t ↦ exp_{γ0}(tγ'0) on [0,1], and a membership criterion for expDom. B: abstract manifold, LC connection, exp via geodesics on the CLOSED [0,1] (velocity within [0,1], HEq): (i) exp_q v = γ(1) and exp_q(tv) = γ(t) on [0,1], (ii) uniqueness of such γ on [0,1], (iii) exp_q defined for ‖v‖ small. A ⇒ B fails genuinely: B is about an abstract Hausdorff ℝⁿ-manifold with an arbitrary smooth RiemannianBundle and an arbitrary Levi-Civita CovariantDerivative (Milnor's sense), which the project's slice submanifolds with the induced metric do not cover (no Nash embedding, no abstract geodesic theory). B ⇒ A is proved (B_to_A, via RoundTrip/Bridge.lean on the connected components of N, re-modelled on ℝᵐ): B's (ii) gives exp_eq (hence exp_zero, exp_smul); exists_initial_ray and mem_expDom_of_isGeodesicOn add the project's Lemma 10.2 (item V7_6) for extending closed geodesics and for local existence near 0.
